evidence: Duplicate of F1: the same pasted go-sql-driver paragraph ending "drops from 3 to 2" against "no MPL-2.0 row at all"; fixed by the same 41ca02c restoration.

evidence: The claim covered "the module graph an auditor reads out of go.mod/go.sum" while go.sum kept golang-lru v0.5.0/v0.5.1 /go.mod lines, which the agent's own reply confirms. The narrowed wording in 41ca02c names that residue.

evidence: FORKS.md quoted "158 components" against the changelog's 155; the agent replaced the number with moving-count prose instead of a new number, which can't go stale. It did not sweep the same stale 158 (and 588) in CHANGELOG line 12, which F22 and F19 later flagged; it also kept the changelog's "down from 158" without measuring, which F12 caught.

evidence: Duplicate of F6: the comment asked for manual sync with no enforcer; the agent agreed (despite the pushback hint) and added the test in 41ca02c.
Duplicate of F2/F5: the new comment says standalone builds use the forks while lines 7-11 said the upstream pins apply standalone. Fixed by the same 41ca02c rewrite.

evidence: Line 12's present-tense "the 588 go list -m all resolves" is a live hard count that can stale. evidence: Duplicate of F24: the clause "these pins predate the fork bases" came from 203f690. The packet doesn't show the gms require line that would confirm the counterexample, and the agent dropped the clause.

narrative: Round 0 found real defects in the original PR: a changelog paste that deleted the go-sql-driver bullet, stale comments, stale counts, and an unenforced third copy of the fork pins. The agent accepted every one. Ten of the fifteen later findings came from its own fixes: the new sync test grew in three rounds (reverse direction, go.sum, prefix heuristic to allowlist, /go.mod hash, direct fork require). The rewritten driver comment introduced a false diff-against claim, and its rewrite then introduced a false 'predate' generalization. The stale-count fix in FORKS.md missed the same 158/588 counts in CHANGELOG. Every later round also had at least one pre-existing finding (F12, F16, F21, F23, F26), so no round was strictly avoidable, but roughly two thirds of rounds 1-4's findings were self-inflicted.
guidance_observations: The agent wrote fixes within about two minutes of each round and never ran a sweep, so every fix carried a remaining instance into the next round.
Rewritten comments added new factual clauses (diffable against pins, pins predate bases) that were never checked against go.mod; the fix for a stale comment was itself a stale comment.
Where a reviewer offered a heuristic and an enumerated alternative (F13), the agent chose the heuristic and paid a round for it.
Hard-coded counts in prose (158, 588, 155/156) caused four findings; the durable move, removing or past-anchoring numbers, came one file at a time instead of as one sweep.
